clue.text: Enough musicians to have a row?

definitions.text: Enough musicians to have a row?

parts.words: Enough musicians to have a row?
parts.note: a rowing crew is eight, so a group of musicians that size could man a racing boat

explanation.surface: A wry question about how many players it takes to start an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is rowing: a racing crew has eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians is the musical term for an ensemble of that size.

clue.text: Attentive old boy — civil type too

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a civil servant is a government official

explanation.surface: A former pupil who is also a government official and pays attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A civil servant is a British government official; 'civil' asks for that phrase's second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick to notice things, alert and watchful.

clue.text: Kipling's liner a lady — but in song the lady's this

definitions.text: Kipling's liner a lady — but in song the lady's this

parts.words: Kipling's liner a lady — but in song the lady's this
parts.note: Kipling wrote that the liner she's a lady, while a famous song says the lady is something less respectable

explanation.surface: A contrast between Kipling's ladylike liner and a song's lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Liner She's a Lady' sets a smart liner against a humble cargo boat; the song is 'The Lady Is a Tramp'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo ship on no fixed route, and a vagrant in the song's title.

clue.text: Sole anti-reformer requiring occasional trimming

indicators.note: a reformer reshapes things, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: A man against reform needs cutting down now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-reformer' looks like a political type; 'reformer' rearranges SOLEANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails on the feet grow and must be clipped now and then.

clue.text: Pieces of music — one by an uncivilized person

parts.note: a bar is a measure of written music, and two of them are wanted here
the second bar of music
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some music, and one savage standing by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' is plural, so two BARs are needed; 'by' simply sets I and AN beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute without culture or manners, the old Greek word for a foreigner.

clue.text: A blunder either way

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same from both ends

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A mistake whichever way you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A silly mistake, in informal speech.

clue.text: Leading features of Antony's friends.

parts.note: Antony addresses friends, Romans and countrymen, and the leading feature of a face is the nose

explanation.surface: A remark about the most important traits of Mark Antony's allies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Antony begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen'; the leading feature of a face is the one that sticks out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent hooked noses, said to be typical of ancient Rome's citizens.

clue.text: Country has excellent refreshment place with a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the letters, so they read upwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
a bar serves drinks

explanation.surface: A nation with a fine bar and a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' turns AIBARA upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula region of south-west Asia, used here as a country name.

clue.text: Where TT types buy spirit?

parts.note: TT suggests teetotallers who would never buy spirits, but TT is also the motorcycle races held on an island

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where non-drinkers would buy alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorcycle races on this island in the Irish Sea; 'spirit' hints at its 'man' and at its spirit of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An island in the Irish Sea home to the famous TT motorcycle races.

clue.text: A mute reminder of Godiva's origin — how she appeared

annotationWithheld.why: A mute reminder of Godiva's origin — how she appeared (5): NUDGE is G (Godiva's origin) inside NUDE, but no clue word signals the insertion, so the container has no indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: A mute reminder of Godiva's origin — how she appeared

clue.text: Condition with space traveller's requirement, perhaps

parts.note: state means condition, as in a state of repair
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Someone sets out what a space traveller might need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space traveller' reads as an astronaut, but 'space' belongs with the wordplay; the traveller is a sea passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A private cabin on a ship is what a sea passenger books, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Was indisposed to turn a girl back

annotationWithheld.why: Was indisposed to turn a girl back (5): reversal of DELIA, but the indicator is split as 'turn ... back' around the fodder, which the grammar takes as two indicators on one op
annotationWithheld.clue: Was indisposed to turn a girl back

clue.text: TV item about fuel

parts.note: re is Latin for 'in the matter of', meaning about
peat is dug turf burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A television piece concerning energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun programme shown on television a second time.

clue.text: Not a diet to replace medicine

indicators.note: to replace asks for the letters to be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to take drugs instead of dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' is the anagram signal working on NOTADIET.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy taken to counteract a poison is a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Feigned to embrace test opener, being excited

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: simulated means feigned or faked

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone pretended to welcome the first batsman and got worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test opener' suggests the opening batsman in a cricket Test match, but it is just the first letter of 'test'.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused or stirred up into activity.

clue.text: Notes explanation given by priest

parts.note: A and B are two musical notes
a solution is the explanation of a problem

explanation.surface: Someone receives notes and an explanation from a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'given by priest', describing what a priest grants after confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest after confession.

clue.text: Still appears without resource?

definitions.meaning: not moving, as if without any shift of position

explanation.surface: A motionless person who seems to have no resources.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: something still is literally lacking shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy and lacking enterprise; and, read whimsically, motionless.

clue.text: Pip's companion in the novel?

parts.note: Pip reads the same both ways, so its companion would be another such name, and one that is a novel title

explanation.surface: A question about who goes with the hero of Great Expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip suggests Dickens, but the link is that the name reads the same backwards; the answer is too, and is a Jane Austen novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A name that reads the same both ways, like Pip, and the title of Austen's novel.

clue.text: This share is expected to produce a yield

definitions.text: This share is expected to produce a yield

parts.words: This share is expected to produce a yield
parts.note: share and yield suggest stocks paying dividends, but the plot is a rented garden growing vegetables

explanation.surface: An investor's comment on a stock that should pay a dividend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an allotment is a small plot of council land rented for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion handed out, and a rented garden plot that grows crops.

clue.text: Heavenly body gets tired, so a replacement's needed

indicators.note: a replacement is needed means the letters must be placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has worn out a part, so a new one must be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement's needed' rearranges TIREDSOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rocky body orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Dog or part of one

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a dog has one at the back that wags

explanation.surface: A dog, or a piece of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow a person, and the wagging rear part of a hound.

clue.text: Objective plan is more involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A neutral scheme that is more complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles PLANISMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached and without personal feeling, as an objective view is.

clue.text: A number give way and agree

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to cede is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: Several people yield and consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent to a request or demand.

clue.text: Summon back law-breaker to get bag

indicators.note: the law is broken open so another piece can sit inside it

parts.note: a rule is a law

indicators.note: back means the word for summon is written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to summon to court

explanation.surface: Recall a criminal to collect a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law-breaker' looks like a criminal, but it is RULE broken open by ETIC, the reverse of CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small drawstring handbag once carried by women.

clue.text: Invested by two small boys

parts.note: Rob is a short form of the name Robert
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Two little lads put money into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' looks financial, but it means dressed in robes of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothed in ceremonial garments, as when someone is installed in office.

clue.text: Go into piano trade, possibly :

indicators.note: into means the piano letter goes inside the other letters
possibly signals that the word trade may be rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Someone considers going into the business of selling pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TRADE to DEART, and 'into' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave or set off is to go.

clue.text: Wasn't there a defence for a criminal?

definitions.text: Wasn't there a defence for a criminal?

parts.words: Wasn't there a defence for a criminal?
parts.note: the plea of being elsewhere, so the accused was not at the scene

explanation.surface: A question about whether a criminal had any defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasn't there' doubles as the defence itself: the claim of being somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: A free rendering of "dry"

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A loose translation of the word dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering of' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched, with no moisture.

clue.text: Note once sent by a pope

definitions.meaning: an old long note in music, now rarely used
a papal letter, less formal than a bull

explanation.surface: A note that a pope once sent.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note of old double length, and a papal letter or brief.

clue.text: / Intimidate site arranger about mistake

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other word
arranger signals the letters of site put in a new order

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A man who lays out building sites threatens someone over a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranger' rearranges SITE to T...ISE, which goes 'about' ERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten or bully with threats.

clue.text: Underworld was apt to be affected by inflation

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
tended means was inclined or apt

explanation.surface: The underworld was likely to be hit by rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests economics, but it is physical swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen or stretched out, as something blown up is.

clue.text: Meaning a lot of snow for instance

definitions.meaning: the gist or general sense of what is said

definitions.text: a lot of snow for instance
definitions.meaning: a heap of snow blown by the wind

explanation.surface: A remark about meaning heavy snow, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The general sense of a speech, and a bank of snow piled by wind.
